messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming-responses-prod high tail-latency and increased inflight queue depth. Metric: streaming_latency_p95 > 1200ms for 3m. Pager: oncall-elena. Link to graphs: https://metrics.redwood.internal/streams/2893123456

oncall-elena: I’m seeing sustained queuing on the streaming workers, GPU memory spikes on a subset of pods. Errors are mostly `EPIPE` and `write timeout` from mux. Latency SLOs breached for a handful of customers.

sam-ml: Can we flip streaming -> buffered for non-critical routes? We have buffered endpoints that fall back to chunked polling. That should reduce KV cache pressure.

jess-platform: Agreed. Runbook options: 1) toggle feature flag global 2) gradually route by tenant (route table) 3) rate-limit SSE frames per connection. Quickest is feature flag.

oncall-elena: I want to avoid full global slam without customer comms. Plan: disable streaming for non-enterprise tenants (percent rollout ~85%), enable short polling fallback, monitor p95/p99. If stable for 10m, we can expand or keep until load subsides.

mike-sre: I can apply the flag. Using `redwoodctl` to scope to tenant groups. Command below, will announce when done.

```bash
# disable streaming for public tier
redwoodctl feature set streaming_push_enabled=false --scope public --env prod
# quick healthcheck
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/health | jq .streams
```

mike-sre: Ran the command, API returned 200. Feature flag propagation in progress. Checking worker logs.

oncall-elena: Nice. Also set temporary rate limit on streaming route to 20fps per connection as a belt-and-suspenders measure. Jess, can you apply shape policy?

jess-platform: Applying shaping policy now: `route: /v1/responses/stream -> rate_limit: 20fps, burst: 5` in prod config. Pushing rollout to 100% within 30s.

mike-sre: Logs: I see a drop in inflight on streaming-controller from 2400 -> 600 in last 90s. p95 went 1200ms -> 280ms. Errors `EPIPE` down 78%. :thumbsup:

karen-support: Which customers will be impacted by this non-enterprise disable? We need to tell support and surface to affected accounts.

amy-sales: I pulled a list: customers with public-tier streaming are AcmeCorp, BetaApps, and three smaller sandbox users. I'll kick off an email and post a short status update to each. Suggest wording: "temporary pause to streaming responses to improve latency; no change to text generation APIs; ETA 2-6 hours."

oncall-elena: Good. Karen, please post in #support with the list and template. Also pin a short note in the status page ticket INC-2893.

karen-support: Posting now. Ticket INC-2893 updated with mitigation details and initial customer list.

ops-bot: Deploy event: streaming-flag-update succeeded on 12/12 pods. Shape policy rollout succeeded on 15/15 route proxies.

mike-sre: Quick check: running a dry-run for upgrade rollback steps in case of regressions. Steps: 1) revert feature flag 2) remove shape policy 3) scale up streaming-workers if needed. I'll keep the revert ready.

oncall-elena: After 10m stable, we'll reassess. If p95 under 500ms and error rate stable, keep the targeted disable until morning. If anything gets worse, revert immediately.

sam-ml: Also note we’ve disabled streaming for background long-poll eval endpoints — this will affect continuous eval harnesses. Sam, pls notify the eval infra owners.

sam-ml: Noted, pinged @eval-team and they acknowledged. They’ll throttle job runs during the window.

amy-sales: I’ll send a proactive note to AcmeCorp with our status page link and estimated ETA.

mike-sre: Monitoring: p95 stream latency, streaming_inflight, worker_cpu, epipe_errors. Dashboards green in the last 5m.

oncall-elena: Handoff: I need to go offline in 25m. Mike, please take primary mitigation ownership afterwards. I’ll document current state in the incident ticket and leave follow-ups for support.

mike-sre: Taking over. I will watch for regression, keep revert plan hot, and coordinate with platform to re-enable with a safer rollout (tenant-by-tenant) once stable.

oncall-elena: Thanks, team. Final asks before I go: 1) support post up 2) sales notify top 3 customers 3) set a 2h follow-up in the incident ticket.

karen-support: Support post complete. Link: https://support.redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2893

amy-sales: Emails sent to AcmeCorp and BetaApps.

incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty escalation paused for streaming-responses-prod during active mitigation window. Remember to reopen if errors spike >2x baseline.

mike-sre: I’m going to keep the flag off for now and continue monitoring. Will update the thread if we change state.

oncall-elena: Handoff complete — leaving to Mike. Logging off. :wave:

mike-sre: Acknowledged. Continuing watch. If any customer impact complaints come in, tag me and I'll join.

ops-bot: Incident log entry created: INC-2893 | mitigation: streaming_push disabled (public) + route shaping | owner: mike-sre

mike-sre: 10m check: p95 270ms, inflight 520, epipe errors back to baseline. Keeping mitigation until 04:00 UTC and then plan a controlled re-enable with 10% tenant ramp.

oncall-elena: Perfect. Good job everyone.
